problem.summary: 如何将注意力机制有效地整合到深度卷积神经网络中，以提升图像分类性能，同时保持网络的可扩展性和训练稳定性。

motivation.summary: 现有的注意力机制方法（如空间变换器）在复杂数据集上存在局限性，例如需要指数级的通道数来捕捉多种注意力类型，且单次注意力修改可能失败。此外，直接堆叠注意力模块会导致性能下降。

core_idea.summary: 提出残差注意力网络（Residual Attention Network），通过堆叠注意力模块（Attention Modules）生成注意力感知特征，并引入注意力残差学习（Attention Residual Learning）机制来训练非常深的网络。

method.summary: 网络由多个注意力模块堆叠而成。每个注意力模块包含一个主干分支（trunk branch）和一个软掩码分支（soft mask branch）。软掩码分支采用自底向上-自顶向下的前馈结构生成注意力掩码，通过公式 H_i,c(x) = (1 + M_i,c(x)) * F_i,c(x) 实现注意力残差学习，其中 M 是掩码，F 是主干特征。

experiments.summary: 在CIFAR-10、CIFAR-100和ImageNet数据集上进行了广泛实验。验证了注意力残差学习、不同掩码结构、噪声标签鲁棒性等。与ResNet、Inception等基线方法进行了比较。

claims.claim: 注意力残差学习机制能够有效训练非常深的残差注意力网络，并提升性能。
堆叠的注意力模块能够捕捉混合注意力（mixed attention），自适应地调整特征。
残差注意力网络在图像分类任务上达到了当时的最优性能，同时具有更高的参数和计算效率。
该网络对噪声标签具有鲁棒性。
自底向上-自顶向下的编码器-解码器掩码结构优于局部卷积结构。

limitations.limitation: 论文未明确讨论该方法在目标检测、语义分割等下游任务中的具体应用效果，也未详细分析注意力掩码的可解释性。

nodes.title: 输入图像
nodes.label: Input
nodes.description: 输入图像经过预处理后送入网络。

nodes.title: 预处理残差单元
nodes.label: Pre-processing Residual Units
nodes.summary: 在注意力模块之前进行特征预处理的残差单元。
nodes.description: 每个注意力模块前有 p 个预处理残差单元。

nodes.title: 注意力模块
nodes.label: Attention Module
nodes.summary: 网络的核心构建块，包含主干分支和软掩码分支，用于生成注意力感知特征。
nodes.description: 由主干分支（trunk branch）和软掩码分支（soft mask branch）组成。软掩码分支通过自底向上-自顶向下结构生成注意力掩码 M(x)，并与主干特征 F(x) 结合，通过注意力残差学习公式 H = (1+M)*F 输出特征。

nodes.title: 主干分支
nodes.label: Trunk Branch
nodes.summary: 注意力模块中的特征提取主干，由多个残差单元组成。
nodes.description: 包含 t 个残差单元，负责提取特征 F(x)。

nodes.title: 软掩码分支
nodes.label: Soft Mask Branch
nodes.summary: 生成注意力掩码的分支，采用自底向上-自顶向下结构。
nodes.description: 通过多次最大池化（下采样）和线性插值（上采样）来扩大感受野并生成掩码。包含 r 个残差单元。最终通过 sigmoid 函数输出范围在 [0,1] 的掩码 M(x)。

nodes.title: 注意力残差学习
nodes.label: Attention Residual Learning
nodes.summary: 核心训练机制，通过修改输出公式 H=(1+M)*F 来稳定训练并提升性能。
nodes.description: 将掩码 M(x) 的范围约束在 [0,1]，当 M(x) 接近 0 时，输出 H(x) 近似于原始特征 F(x)，从而保持主干分支的良好性质（如残差单元的恒等映射），避免性能下降。

nodes.title: 混合注意力
nodes.label: Mixed Attention
nodes.summary: 论文中表现最佳的注意力类型，掩码对每个通道和空间位置独立使用 sigmoid 激活。
nodes.description: 激活函数 f1(x_i,c) = 1 / (1 + exp(-x_i,c))，不对掩码施加额外约束，让注意力随特征自适应变化。

nodes.title: 输出特征
nodes.label: Output Features
nodes.summary: 经过注意力模块增强后的特征，用于后续分类。
nodes.description: 注意力模块的输出 H(x) 作为下一层的输入或最终分类的特征。

deltas.before: 直接堆叠注意力模块会导致性能下降，因为掩码与特征的点积会逐层降低特征值，且可能破坏主干分支的良好性质（如恒等映射）。
deltas.after: 引入注意力残差学习，将输出公式修改为 H = (1 + M) * F。当 M 接近 0 时，输出近似原始特征，从而保持主干分支的性质，稳定训练。
deltas.why_it_matters: 使得网络可以堆叠数百层注意力模块而性能持续提升，解决了深度注意力网络的训练难题。

deltas.before: 使用单一网络分支生成注意力掩码（如空间变换器）。
deltas.after: 采用堆叠的注意力模块，每个模块有自己的掩码分支，可以捕捉不同层次的注意力（如低层颜色特征、高层部件特征），并逐步精炼注意力。
deltas.why_it_matters: 能够处理复杂图像中多种类型的注意力需求，避免了单一掩码分支需要指数级通道数的问题，并提供了多次修正注意力的机会。

deltas.before: 掩码分支可能采用局部卷积等简单结构。
deltas.after: 掩码分支采用自底向上-自顶向下的编码器-解码器结构，通过多次池化和插值来扩大感受野，捕捉多尺度信息。
deltas.why_it_matters: 实验表明，编码器-解码器结构比局部卷积结构能获得更低的测试误差（5.52% vs 6.48%），说明多尺度信息对软注意力优化有益。

variables.name: H_{i,c}(x)
variables.description: 注意力模块的输出特征，位于空间位置 i，通道 c。

variables.name: M_{i,c}(x)
variables.description: 软掩码分支生成的注意力掩码，范围在 [0, 1]。

formulas.intuition: 这是注意力残差学习的核心公式。通过将掩码 M 加 1 后与主干特征 F 相乘，当 M 接近 0 时，输出 H 近似于原始特征 F，从而保持了主干分支的良好性质（如残差连接的恒等映射），使得网络可以稳定地堆叠很深。这不同于原始的残差学习 H = x + F(x)，这里的 F(x) 是深层卷积网络生成的特征，而 M(x) 作为特征选择器，增强好特征，抑制噪声。

variables.name: f_1
variables.description: 混合注意力（Mixed Attention）的激活函数。

variables.name: x_{i,c}
variables.description: 掩码分支最后一层的特征值。

formulas.intuition: 对掩码分支的输出应用标准的 sigmoid 函数，将值压缩到 (0, 1) 区间。这种混合注意力不对空间或通道维度施加额外约束，让注意力掩码随特征自适应变化，实验表明其性能最佳。

variables.name: Q
variables.description: 用于模拟标签噪声的混淆矩阵。

variables.name: r
variables.description: 干净标签的比例（clean label ratio）。

formulas.intuition: 在噪声标签鲁棒性实验中使用的混淆矩阵。对角线元素为 r，表示标签正确的概率；非对角线元素为 (1-r)/9，表示标签被随机错误替换为其他9个类别之一的概率。用于生成不同噪声水平的训练数据。

main_result.experiment: ImageNet 分类 (单模型单裁剪)
main_result.result: Attention-92 达到 19.5% 的 top-1 错误率和 4.8% 的 top-5 错误率，相比 ResNet-200 提升了 0.6% 的 top-1 准确率，且主干深度仅为 ResNet-200 的 46%，前向 FLOPs 为 69%。

ablation.experiment: 注意力残差学习 (ARL) vs 朴素注意力学习 (NAL)
ablation.result: 在 CIFAR-10 上，使用 ARL 的 Attention-56/92/128/164 均显著优于使用 NAL 的对应网络。例如 Attention-164 使用 ARL 误差为 4.31%，使用 NAL 为 7.18%。

ablation.experiment: 不同掩码结构：编码器-解码器 vs 局部卷积
ablation.result: 在 CIFAR-10 上，Attention-Encoder-Decoder-56 误差为 5.52%，优于 Attention-Local-Conv-56 的 6.48%。

ablation.experiment: 不同注意力类型：混合注意力、通道注意力、空间注意力
ablation.result: 在 CIFAR-10 上，混合注意力 (f1) 误差为 5.52%，优于通道注意力 (f2, 6.24%) 和空间注意力 (f3, 6.33%)。

robustness.result: 在 CIFAR-10 上，使用不同噪声水平（干净标签比例 r）训练，Attention-92 的测试误差始终显著低于 ResNet-164。例如在 r=0.8 时，Attention-92 误差为 6.28%，ResNet-164 为 7.32%。

scaling.result: 通过增加每个阶段的注意力模块数量 m（从1到4），网络深度从 Attention-56 增加到 Attention-164，在使用 ARL 时性能持续提升（误差从 5.52% 降至 4.31%）。

case_study.result: 图1展示了热气球图像的注意力掩码示例：天空掩码抑制了低层背景蓝色特征，气球实例掩码突出了高层气球底部特征。

efficiency.result: Attention-56 (31.9M 参数, 6.3G FLOPs) 相比 ResNet-152 (60.2M 参数, 11.3G FLOPs) 参数减少 47%，FLOPs 减少 44%，且 top-1 错误率更低 (21.76% vs 22.16%)。

terms.definition: 残差注意力网络的基本构建单元，包含一个主干分支和一个软掩码分支，用于生成注意力感知特征。

terms.term: 注意力残差学习 (Attention Residual Learning, ARL)
terms.definition: 一种训练机制，通过公式 H = (1+M)*F 将注意力掩码 M 与主干特征 F 结合，使得当 M 接近 0 时输出近似原始特征，从而稳定深层网络的训练。
注意力模块中生成连续注意力掩码的分支，通常采用自底向上-自顶向下的编码器-解码器结构。
注意力模块中负责提取主要特征的分支，由多个残差单元组成。
一种注意力类型，其掩码对每个通道和空间位置独立使用 sigmoid 激活函数，不施加额外约束，让注意力随特征自适应变化。

terms.term: 朴素注意力学习 (Naive Attention Learning, NAL)
terms.definition: 作为对比的基线方法，指直接堆叠注意力模块而不使用注意力残差学习机制。

required_models: 预训练的 ResNet 或从头训练
reproduction.compute_requirements: 论文未明确给出，但根据网络规模（如 Attention-92 有 51.3M 参数）和 ImageNet 训练迭代次数（530k 次），推测需要多 GPU 训练数天。

steps.description: 1. 实现基础残差单元（Residual Unit）和预激活残差单元。
2. 实现软掩码分支，包括自底向上（多次最大池化）和自顶向下（线性插值上采样）结构，以及跳跃连接。
3. 实现注意力模块，组合主干分支和软掩码分支，并应用注意力残差学习公式 H = (1+M)*F。
4. 按照论文描述的架构（如 Table 2）堆叠多个注意力模块，构建完整的残差注意力网络（如 Attention-56, Attention-92）。
5. 在 CIFAR-10/100 上训练，使用论文指定的优化器（Nesterov SGD）、学习率调度（初始 0.1，在 64k, 96k 迭代除以 10，总迭代 160k）和数据增强。
6. 在 ImageNet 上训练，使用论文指定的学习率调度（在 200k, 400k, 500k 迭代除以 10，总迭代 530k）和输入尺寸（如 224x224 或 320x320）。
7. 进行消融实验：对比 ARL 与 NAL、不同掩码结构、不同注意力类型。
8. 进行噪声标签鲁棒性实验，按照论文公式 (7) 生成带噪声标签的数据集。

metadata.title: Residual Attention Network for Image Classification
metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / Pose Estimation / Computer Vision / Attention / Computer Vision / CNN / Computer Vision / Top-cited Computer Vision paper
metadata.abstract: In this work, we propose Residual Attention Network, a convolutional neural network using attention mechanism which can incorporate with state-of-art feed forward network architecture in an end-to-end training fashion. Our Residual Attention Network is built by stacking Attention Modules which generate attention-aware features. The attention-aware features from different modules change adaptively as layers going deeper. Inside each Attention Module, bottom-up top-down feedforward structure is used to unfold the feedforward and feedback attention process into a single feedforward process. Importantly, we propose attention residual learning to train very deep Residual Attention Networks which can be easily scaled up to hundreds of layers. Extensive analyses are conducted on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets to verify the effectiveness of every module mentioned above. Our Residual Attention Network achieves state-of-the-art object recognition performance on three benchmark datasets including CIFAR-10 (3.90% error), CIFAR-100 (20.45% error) and ImageNet (4.8% single model and single crop, top-5 error). Note that, our method achieves 0.6% top-1 accuracy improvement with 46% trunk depth and 69% forward FLOPs comparing to ResNet-200. The experiment also demonstrates that our network is robust against noisy labels.

Abstract

In this work, we propose “Residual Attention Network”, a convolutional neural network using attention mechanism which can incorporate with state-of-art feed forward net- work architecture in an end-to-end training fashion. Our Residual Attention Network is built by stacking Attention Modules which generate attention-aware features. The attention-aware features from different modules change adaptively as layers going deeper . Inside each Attention Module, bottom-up top-down feedforward structure is used to unfold the feedforward and feedback attention process into a single feedforward process. Importantly, we propose attention residual learning to train very deep Residual At- tention Networks which can be easily scaled up to hundreds of layers. Extensive analyses are conducted on CIF AR-10 and CIF AR-100 datasets to verify the effectiveness of every mod- ule mentioned above. Our Residual Attention Network achieves state-of-the-art object recognition performance on three benchmark datas...
Apart from more discriminative feature representation

brought by the attention mechanism, our model also ex- hibits following appealing properties: (1) Increasing Attention Modules lead to consistent perfor- mance improvement, as different types of attention are cap- tured extensively. Fig.1 shows an example of different types of attentions for a hot air balloon image. The sky attention
mask diminishes background responses while the balloon

instance mask highlighting the bottom part of the balloon. (2) It is able to incorporate with state-of-the-art deep net- work structures in an end-to-end training fashion. Specif- ically, the depth of our network can be easily extended to hundreds of layers. Our Residual Attention Network out- performs state-of-the-art residual networks on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and challenging ImageNet [5] image classiﬁca- tion dataset with signiﬁcant reduction of computation (69% forward FLOPs). All of the aforementioned properties, which are chal- lenging to achieve with previous approaches, are made pos- sible with following contributions: (1) Stacked network structure: Our Residual Attention Net- work is constructed by stacking multiple Attention Mod- ules. The stacked structure is the basic application of mixed attention mechanism. Thus, different types of attention are able to be captured in different Attention Modules. arXiv:1704.06904v1 [cs.CV] 23 Apr 2017

Therefore, we propose attention residual learning mecha- nism to optimize very deep Residual Attention Network with hundreds of layers. (3) Bottom-up top-down feedforward attention : Bottom-up top-down feedforward structure has been successfully ap- plied to human pose estimation [24] and image segmenta- tion [22, 25, 1]. We use such structure as part of Attention Module to add soft weights on features. This structure can mimic bottom-up fast feedforward process and top-down attention feedback in a single feedforward process which allows us to develop an end-to-end trainable network with top-down attention. The bottom-up top-down structure in our work differs from stacked hourglass network [24] in its intention of guiding feature learning. 2. Related Work Evidenc...

rones are updated with top information and have inﬂuence on the feedforward process during training [2, 30]. How- ever, a new process, reinforcement learning [30] or opti- mization [2] is involved during the training step. Highway Network [29] extends control gate to solve gradient degra- dation problem for deep convolutional neural network. However, recent advances of image classiﬁcation focus on training feedforward convolutional neural networks us- ing “very deep” structure [27, 33, 10]. The feedforward convolutional network mimics the bottom-up paths of hu- man cortex. Various approaches have been proposed to
further improve the discriminative ability of deep convolu-

tional neural network. VGG [27], Inception [33] and resid- ual learning [10] are proposed to train very deep neural networks. Stochastic depth [14], Batch Normalization [15] and Dropout [28] exploit regularization for convergence and avoiding overﬁtting and degradation. Soft attention developed in recent work [3, 17] can be trained end-to-end for convolutional network. Our Resid- ual Attention Network incorporates the soft attention in fast developing feedforward network structure in an innova- tive way. Recent proposed spatial transformer module [17] achieves state-of-the-art results on house number recogni- tion task. A deep network module capturing top informa- tion is used to generate afﬁne transformation. The afﬁne transformation is applied to the input image to get attended region and then feed to another deep network module. The whole process can be trained end-to-end by using differen- tiable network layer which performs spatial transformation. Attention to scale [3] uses soft...

In Attention Modules, the attention mask can not only serve as a feature selector during forward inference, but also as a gradient update ﬁlter during back propagation. In the soft mask branch, the gradient of mask for input feature is: ∂M (x,θ )T (x,φ )

Mask branches can prevent wrong gradients (from noisy labels) to update trunk param- eters. Experiment in Sec.4.1 shows the robustness of our Residual Attention Network against noisy labels. Instead of stacking Attention Modules in our design, a simple approach would be using a single network branch to generate soft weight mask, similar to spatial transformer layer [17]. However, these methods have several drawbacks on challenging datasets such as ImageNet. First, images
with clutter background, complex scenes, and large appear-

ance variations need to be modeled by different types of attentions. In this case, features from different layers need to be modeled by different attention masks. Using a single mask branch would require exponential number of channels to capture all combinations of different factors. Second, a single Attention Module only modify the features once. If the modiﬁcation fails on some parts of the image, the fol- lowing network modules do not get a second chance. The Residual Attention Network alleviates above prob- lems. In Attention Module, each trunk branch has its own mask branch to learn attention that is specialized for its fea- tures. As shown in Fig.1, in hot air balloon images, blue color features from bottom layer have corresponding sky
mask to eliminate background, while part features from top
layer are reﬁned by balloon instance mask. Besides, the in- cremental nature of stacked network structure can gradually reﬁne attention for complex images.

First, dot production with mask range from zero to one repeatedly will degrade the value of features in deep layers. Second, soft mask can potentially break good property of trunk branch, for example, the iden- tical mapping of Residual Unit. We propose attention residual learning to ease the above problems. Similar to ideas in residual learning, if soft mask unit can be constructed as identical mapping, the perfor- mances should be no worse than its counterpart without at- tention. Thus we modify outputH of Attention Module as

imates the residual function. In our formulation, Fi,c(x) indicates the features generated by deep convolutional net- works. The key lies on our mask branches M (x). They work as feature selectors which enhance good features and suppress noises from trunk features. In addition, stacking Attention Modules backs up atten- tion residual learning by its incremental nature. Attention residual learning can keep good properties of original fea- tures, but also gives them the ability to bypass soft mask branch and forward to top layers to weaken mask branch’s feature selection ability. Stacked Attention Modules can gradually reﬁne the feature maps. As show in Fig.1, fea- tures become much clearer as depth going deeper. By using attention residual learning, increasing depth of the proposed Residual Attention Network can improve performance con- sistently. As shown in the experiment section, the depth of Residual Attention Network is increased up to 452 whose
performance surpasses ResNet-1001 by a large margin on

CIFAR dataset. 3.2. Soft Mask Branch Following previous attention mechanism idea in DBN [21], our mask branch contains fast feed-forward sweep and top-down feedback steps. The former operation quickly collects global information of the whole image, the latter operation combines global information with original feature maps. In convolutional neural network, the two steps unfold into bottom-up top-down fully convolutional structure.
From input, max pooling are performed several times to

After reaching the lowest resolution, the global information is then expanded by a symmetrical top- down architecture to guide input features in each position. Experiments In this section, we evaluate the performance of pro- posed Residual Attention Network on a series of bench- mark datasets including CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 [19], and ImageNet [5]. Our experiments contain two parts. In the ﬁrst part, we analyze the effectiveness of each component in the Residual Attention Network including attention residual

learning mechanism and different architectures of soft mask branch in the Attention Module. After that, we explore the noise resistance property. Given limited computation re- sources, we choose CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 dataset to conduct these experiments. Finally, we compare our net- work with state-of-the-art results in CIFAR dataset. In the second part, we replace the Residual Unit with Inception Module and ResNeXt to demonstrate our Residual Atten- tion Network surpasses origin networks both in parameter efﬁciency and ﬁnal performance. Above results suggest that our model enjoys high efﬁciency and good performance. 5. Discussion We propose a Residual Attention Network which stacks multiple Attention Modules. The beneﬁts of our network are in two folds: it can capture mixed attention and is an ex- tensible convolutional neural network. The ﬁrst beneﬁt lies in that different Attention Modules capture different types of attention to guide feature learning. Our experiments on the forms of activation function also validate this point: free form mixed attention will have better performance than constrained (including single) attention. The second ben- eﬁt comes from encoding top-down attention mechanism into bot...
Modules can be combined to form larger network structure.

Moreover, residual attention learning allows training very deep Residual Attention Network. The performance of our model surpasses state-of-the-art image classiﬁcation meth- ods, i.e. ResNet on CIFAR-10 (3.90% error), CIFAR-100 (20.67% error), and challenging ImageNet dataset (0.6% top-1 accuracy improvement) with only 46% trunk depth and 69% forward FLOPs (comparing with ResNet-200). In the future, we will exploit different applications of deep Residual Attention Network such as detection and segmen- tation to better explore mixed attention mechanism for spe- ciﬁc tasks.
